newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Pripps Ringnes says Pepsi deal to run 20 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Pripps Ringnes says Pepsi deal to run 20 yrs.

text.p: Norwegian-Swedish beverage group Pripps Ringnes said on Tuesday its cooperation deal with PepsiCo would run for 20 years from January 1, 2001.

The group said on Monday it had reached an agreement with PepsiCo about production, distribution and sale of Pepsi-Cola and 7UP in Sweden, starting in 2001 when PepsiCo's deal with its current Swedish partner Spendrups expires.
Spendrups's president Jens Spendrup said on Tuesday that PepsiCo had promised to continue cooperating with his company after the year 2000, but PepsiCo denied this.
Spendrups has not yet decided how it would go about defending the deal, Jens Spendrup said.

Pepsi products account for about 15 percent of Spendrups's earnings, and about 20 percent of its volumes, he said. But the loss of the PepsiCo link caused its share price to fall on Tuesday, dipping 3.50 to 56 crowns.
Pripps Ringnes declined to disclose details of the new deal, but spokesman Goran Orre told Reuters on Tuesday that both parties will benefit from higher sales volumes.
PepsiCo's sales volumes are currently around one-third of Coca-Cola's volumes in Sweden, Orre said. Coca-Cola products have total annual volume of about 200 million litres in Sweden.
"Pepsi has about 15 percent of the soft drink market," Orre said. "We expect to increase both market share and volumes significantly."
Pripps Ringnes has production in Stockholm and Gothenburg in Sweden as well as nationwide distribution and sales. The cooperation with Pepsi could make all segments more efficient, Orre said.
The companies have also begun preliminary discussions surrounding possible cooperation in Norway, but no agreement has yet been reached, Pripps Ringnes said on Monday.
Pripps Ringnes is owned by Norwegian food-based conglomerate Orkla, whose A-share rose 13.50 Norwegian crowns at 559.50 at 1015 GMT Tuesday.
Spendrups swung to a six-month profit after financial items of 35 million crowns from a loss of 26 million crowns in the corresponding year-earlier period.
